Here we go!

The official Nintendo Sponsored championship, the Pokemon Video Game Championships, consists of two players facing off against one another with Pokemon made and bred to be the best that it can be.The battles conducted will be double battles. Each player is allowed a team of six Lvl 50 Pokemon, and every match each player brings four of the six Pokemon to battle. Official tournaments have a time limit of 15 minutes consisting of turns that last a maximum of 45 seconds. There are certain pokemon that are banned, and there is a list every season of banned pokemon and rule changes. Here is the simplified standard ruleset for the VGC'15 season.

To explain how to make a pokemon competetive, I'll tell you of how the actual Pokemon works.

There are 4 modfiers to a pokemon's stats.

1- Base Stats: The first and foremost is the pokemon's base stats. These values can be potentially any number and never change. They are >unique to the Pokemon's species as a whole.

So, Pikachu A and Pickachu B will have the same base stats, but Pikachu A and Charizard with not.

2- Individual Values: A pokemons individual values (IV's) is a number from 0 to 31 which affect the final number in a Pokemon's stat, 0 being the >lowest possible and 31 being the best possible. These are unique to an individual Pokemon and can never be changed on the >individual Pokemon.

Say Pikachu A has a Sp.Atk IV of 31, and Pikachu B has a Sp.Atk IV of 0. Pikachu A will be dealing a lot more damage with >special attacks than Pikachu B.

3- Effort Value: The effort value (EV) is a number that can be changes >any number of times over a Pokemon's lifetime. A Pokemon can gain EV's by battling other Pokemon or by using items. >Each stat can have a maximum of 252 EV's, with a Pokemon's total EV's having a maximum number of 508. At level 100, >every 4 EV's in a stat will add 1 point to the stat.

Applying this, say Pikachu A and Pikachu B both have a 31 in their Sp.Atk IV's. Both will be dealing the same damage right? >WRONG. Pikachu A has 252 EV's in Sp.Atk and Pikachu B doesn't have any! Pikachu A will deal more damage.

4- Nature: A Pokemon's nature add's 10% to one of its stats, but subtracts >10% from a different stat. This is also unique to individual Pokemon and cannot be changed. This looks like the simplest >part, but 10% really adds a lot and can swing a game!

Back to our Pikachu's. OH LOOK! Pikachu A and B both have a 31 in their Sp.Atk IV's and 252 EV's in the same stat! >Pikachu A has a +Sp.Atk -Atk Nature though, and Pikachu B has a +Atk -Sp.Atk nature. Pikachu A will still be dealing more >damage!

Competetive players use in game mechanics and the Pokemon daycare to breed Pokemon to suit their teams needs. With 719 Pokemon, 4 moves for each of these pokemon, 621 total moves, 21 natures, infinite EV and IV combinations, and a luck factor, this game can get pretty crazy. Don't be afraid! Jump in!
